full_details: At nine you put the pointing in Augustine's hand. Friday is what he asked, and this morning is soon enough. You did not copy a verse onto the sheet. You open Errors, and then you are idle till the end. French Doctor was the Rose. You did not go. After the play the almanac was open. It is new moon. Lent begins on the fifth of March, which is five playing weeks. John has twenty-eight afternoons before Lent, and he wants four of them for the comedy. Richard wants three full weeks for Berowne, for he never stops talking. You fixed Thursday the twentieth of February, a term-less day, and you trust the Inns to come anyway. Kemp asked what jig follows. A comedy needs none. That was the first small cloud. You stop on Shrove Tuesday, the fourth of March, rather than play into Lent and tempt the Mayor. Pope said the Rose will play till they're stopped. John said the Rose has no mayor sleeping next door to its poet. The company's stop is not your answer to Anne. You still do not know the day.
one_sentence: You gave Augustine the songs in the morning, opened Errors, and after the play the sharers fixed Thursday the twentieth and a stop on Shrove Tuesday.
title: Gave Augustine the pointing and fixed the twentieth
